# @scaffold: Turn the problem folder's Design.txt into compiling Java in <folder>/main, with EXACTLY its classes and signatures and TODO bodies. Nothing it doesn't name.

Usage: `@scaffold <problem folder> [optional: only a part, e.g. "EvictionPolicy only"]`
(If the arguments don't come through, use `@.kiro/prompts/scaffold.md <arguments>` instead.)

Arguments: $ARGUMENTS
(If the line above shows a placeholder instead of real arguments, my arguments are the rest of my message.)

Scaffold from Design.txt. Arguments: the arguments above

**Folder.** The first argument is the problem folder if it is a folder; otherwise run
`./lld.sh list` and take the only or newest one. Say which in your first line. If it has no
`pom.xml`, run `./lld.sh init <folder>`. Read `<folder>/Design.txt` (any capitalisation) and the
Java already in `<folder>/main/`. Never edit Design.txt.

**Create, in `<folder>/main/<pkg path>/`** (package rule in AGENTS.md), exactly what Design.txt
declares and nothing else:
- every class, interface, enum, record and exception it names, with the declared fields;
- every method and constructor with the declared signature, character for character: names,
  parameter types and order, return types, generics, `throws`;
- constructors and setup methods that only store or validate arguments get real bodies (argument
  checks the FRs state, field assignment). Every method that implements an FR rule gets
  `throw new UnsupportedOperationException("TODO FR-n: <that FR's text, shortened>");`, naming the
  FR(s) it serves;
- enums with transitions get the transition table and `canTransitionTo`;
- no Manager, Orchestrator, Service, Repository, Facade, Demo or extra interface unless
  Design.txt names it; no class that only forwards calls.

If a declared signature can't satisfy an FR as written (the FR says a value is returned, the
signature returns `void`), use the signature the FR needs, mark it
`// DRIFT: <declared> -> <new>, because FR-n: <why>` as the first line of the method, and say so
at the top of your reply. Anything Design.txt leaves open: make the plain choice and list it.

Do not implement business rules and do not apply patterns beyond the classes Design.txt already
names. Run `./lld.sh compile <folder>` until it is clean.

**Reply with:**
1. the file tree of `<folder>/main`;
2. a table: Design.txt item → file → FR(s) it serves;
3. **Drift**: every DRIFT line you added, or "none"; **Filled gaps**: at most 3 bullets;
4. next step: `@fr-tests <folder>`.
